message.content: The clearest risk management named is supply chain availability, with the company stating that the supply environment is less flexible today than a year ago and that supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. That risk would be confirmed if fourth-quarter revenue came in below $1.93 billion, the bottom of the guided range, rather than at or above the $1.95 billion top of that range [D3]. A second risk is the fading of the one-time tariff impacts that lifted fiscal 2026 profitability, which management said will not repeat and which creates a high comparison bar for future periods [D4]. Confirmation would come from a gross margin below 65.87 percent [D1]. A third risk is that costs grow faster than the revenue they support, since total segment research and development expense rose 24.8 percent, total segment selling, general and administrative expense rose 25.99 percent and total segment cost of products and services rose 21.62 percent [D1]. That would be confirmed by segment operating income growth slowing below 81.36 percent, the growth reported for the segment total [D1]. A fourth risk is the concentration of the growth story in AI infrastructure spending and commercial communications, where wireline revenue surpassed wireless revenue for the first time [D2]. Confirmation would be Communications Solutions Group revenue failing to exceed $1.35 billion [D1]. A fifth risk is the set of demand and policy exposures the company itself lists, including customer purchasing decisions and timing, tariff and trade policy impacts and order cancellations, along with export control regulations and compliance and geopolitical tension and conflict outside the United States [D1]. Those would be confirmed by quarterly revenue below $1.85 billion or a year-over-year revenue growth rate below 36.54 percent [D1].
